targets.authors: Baird, B., Smallwood, J., Mrazek, M. D., Kam, J. W. Y., Franklin, M. S., & Schooler, J. W.
targets.title: Inspired by distraction: Mind wandering facilitates creative incubation.
targets.evidence_quote:
Study 1 attempted to replicate results reported in Baird et al.
(2012) that an increased proportion of mind wandering during an
incubation interval correlates with better AUT performance.
targets.outcome_quote:
However, across 2 studies (N = 443),
we found no evidence for the claim that mind wandering during a creative-incubation interval facilitates
a form of creativity associated with divergent thinking.

reasoning: Two new samples conceptually retest Baird et al. The authors explicitly identify their own attempt as failed across both studies. Smeekens and Kane and Steindorf are earlier attempts discussed and used for design refinements, rather than targets of the present experiments.
